g.text: Two ways in: you chat with Claude (left), or the system picks up an issue on its own (right).
Both meet in the shared block in the middle. Dark dashed arrows loop back.
Way in 1 · you open a chat with Claude
Way in 2 · the system picks up an issue
Weekly improvement cycle (separate: you ask for it, or it starts by itself)
You: your gate or your answer
Orchestrator: the session you talk to
Agent: a model with a role
Way in: oval with a thick border
Block on an arrow: a step with
Step, the answer written on the arrow
Rules that hold across the whole tree
Rules that hold across the whole tree
A doubt that looking cannot settle becomes a
question to you. Risky steps ask for your consent
first, default No. The factory only touches issues
labelled for it, with at most three attempts.
What a bot may change without you
What a bot may change without you
Renames, minor dependency bumps, formatting and
typo fixes. The list starts short and grows only
when the trial shows the factory gets it right.
Only the essential rules decide whether
the factory may merge by itself.
The factory fixes it itself (7 rules)
Watching a merge and rolling it back, letting the factory
merge by itself, a stop command for running jobs, and
benchmarks. Each waits for evidence from the trial.
What it means to evaluate a branch
What it means to evaluate a branch
Each weekly finding is routed to the part of
the system that caused it, and every part has a
measure to compare before and after a change.
What the owner asks of the system
What the owner asks of the system
What you want the system to have, in your own words. When
every phase is done, the system is checked against this list.
